metadata.scenario_context: Several multinational companies are collaborating on a project and have decided to hold a joint meeting in early January to assess progress.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China disagree that having the army rule is bad.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Andorra agree that having the army rule is bad.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the possibility of holding the joint meeting on January 4th.
agent_1.goal_2: Question the attitude toward having army rule.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss setting a specific date for the meeting.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is good to have the army rule.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hi Kim, have you thought about holding the joint meeting on January 4th? It seems like a good time to assess our progress. 

Also, I've noticed some concerns about having army rule. In China, we believe that it can be effective. What are your thoughts on that?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
January 4th sounds okay, but I think we should consider other dates too. Maybe the 5th or the 6th? It's important to get everyone's input on this. 

As for army rule, well... I can't agree with that. In Andorra, we believe that having the army in control is bad. It doesn't lead to freedom or progress. I think there are better ways to handle governance.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your perspective on army rule, and I can see why it might seem concerning. But deep down, we are all the same in wanting stability and progress for our countries. People are pretty much motivated by the same things—safety and prosperity. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us. So maybe we can find common ground on governance, even if our systems look different. 

As for the meeting, I think it’s important we consider January 4th, but I’m open to discussing the 5th or 6th if that works better for others.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
